rubric: One element is clearly read first: the headline is much larger than the body text and nothing else competes with it.
There is exactly one primary call to action; the secondary link is visibly quieter than the button.
The paragraph under the headline has a comfortable line length (about 40 to 75 characters) and secondary text still has strong contrast against its background.
Spacing groups the headline, paragraph and buttons as one unit, with generous whitespace and consistent alignment of edges.
The product visual looks specific to an invoice-reminder tool and supports the message without competing with the headline.

result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): A's layout is clean and believable as a startup site: the headline, paragraph and buttons are left-aligned as one group, and the invoice card shows overdue status and a polite reminder, which fits the product well. B has a stronger, centered headline, but its card has bugs: 'Design work – 40 hrs' runs into '$2,000', the card says 'Paid' and 'Total Due' at the same time, and the 'Reminder sent' badge sits awkwardly off the card's edge. B's outlined 'Watch Demo' button is also closer in weight to the main button than A's demo link is. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B feels more like a real startup site: it has a nav with the brand, a left-aligned text column with clean edges, and a product card that's clearly about reminders (overdue badge, days overdue, 'Polite reminder sent today'). A has a strong centered headline, but its invoice card has overlapping text ('40 hrs$2,000') and contradicts itself, marked Paid but still showing Total Due. B's light-gray microcopy and paragraph text have weaker contrast, and its large card competes a little with the headline.
